text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH SEV - KV-cache / continuous-batching anomaly detected. Spike in NCCL stalls and 99p latency across multi-GPU TP pools. Paging oncall @sasha. Autoscaling triggering hot shards. Links: https://alerts.internal/r/1923456789

sasha: acknowledging, jumping in. what’s the scope? which customers/pools?

jamie: quick summary from metrics: since 12:14 UTC 99p latency went from ~120ms -> ~3.2s on rdx-13b-quant-v2 pools using tp-kv-shard strategy. NCCL stall count up by 340% in 10m. Error rate (502/timeout) ~4% traffic across dedicated clusters pool-dc-eu-3.

tariq: saw noisy logs on two dedicated clusters: cust-omega and cust-pioneer seeing streaming failures. Also noticed uneven shard partitions in KV-placement: GPU0 received ~62% of keys, GPU1 ~18%, GPU2 ~10%, GPU3 ~10% — looks like hashing/placement bug. Example NCCL warn: `NCCL WARN System error: coll net connecting failed (rank 0 -> rank 2)`.

kara: support here — cust-pioneer reported degraded interactive completions and slow streaming. Not yet SLA breach but multiple customer sessions timed out. Notifying customers A/B.

sasha: assign owners. jamie/tariq you two triage runtime side. maria can you get infra to stop autoscale bursts for affected pools to avoid cascading handoffs? kara, populate customer impact table. I'll coordinate handoff.

jamie: preliminary root cause hypothesis: recent change to KV sharding hash function (commit abc1234) intended for evenness + continuous batching optimization changed bucket assignment edge-case when sequence-prefix caching enabled. That interacts badly with TP split logic and causes hot partitioning -> NCCL imbalance -> stalls.

tariq: mitigation plan (live): 1) disable continuous batching for affected pools, 2) force rehash to equal partitions, 3) roll a targeted hotfix that reverts the faulty hash branch. Doing 1 now as low-risk.

jamie: command to flip batching flag (run on control plane):
```
# disable continuous batching for pool-dc-eu-3
rictl config set pool/dc-eu-3/continuous_batching false --env production --reason "emergency: kv-shard imbalance"
```
Applying to canary 5% first.

tariq: applied to canary, watching metrics. canary 5% shows 99p down from 3.2s -> 480ms in 30s. pushing to 50% now.

maria: infra: paused autoscaler for pool-dc-eu-3 to stop additional TP handoffs. scaling suspend id: suspend-192345.

kara: updated impacted customer list: cust-omega (priority), cust-pioneer (priority), cust-horizon (minor). Support page updated and CSMs pinged.

sasha: good. jamie/tariq proceed to rehash and prepare rollback patch for the hash change. We need minimal blast radius. Can we do hot-restart of process shards without full restart?

jamie: yes we can trigger shard rebalance via placement API, non-disruptive. command:
```
rictl kv placement rebalance --pool dc-eu-3 --mode non-disruptive --target-uniform
```
Initiating now. Note: some RPCs will see brief stalls (~100-200ms) during migration windows.

tariq: started rebalance. Observing reallocation: GPU0 load dropping to ~30%, GPUs evenly ~25% each after 90s. NCCL stall count decreasing.

sasha: telemetry check: 1) 99p latency across pool down to 260ms now, 2) error rate from 4% -> 0.6%. customer sessions restoring. Kara, confirm with cust-omega?

kara: cust-omega reports immediate improvement, live sessions resumed, will keep monitoring. No escalations so far.

jamie: while rebalance looks good, we still need code-level revert for hash edge-case. Preparing rollback CL now (revert abc1234 branch). Target patch:
```
--- a/runtime/kv_shard.cc
+++ b/runtime/kv_shard.cc
@@
- int bucket = fancy_hash(key) % shards;
+ int bucket = legacy_hash(key) % shards; // revert temporary change to avoid edge-case
```
Will push to canary pipeline after tests.

maria: note: rolling the CL will require rolling canary then staged rollout over 10m windows to avoid re-triggering pack/unpack storms. I'll coordinate rollout windows.

incident-bot: update: mitigation actions: continuous_batching disabled for pool-dc-eu-3, autoscaler suspended, KV placement rebalance started. Incident severity -> ongoing.

jamie: canary patch deployed to 5% with tests passing. Monitoring for regressions.

tariq: after patch at 5% metrics stable. proceeding 25% then 100% over 15m.

sasha: customer impact assessment: ~6k user-seconds affected across 3 customers, peak error rate 4% for ~14 minutes. Noted as SEV-2 candidate but avoided SLA breaches. Put oncall handoff plan: tay will take monitoring for the next 2 hours.

tay: taking handoff. I'll watch the dashboard and alert channel. If latency resurges, page me.

kara: closing loop with customers: will send summary & ETA for postmortem.

jamie: final metrics after full rollout: 99p latency back to 120-160ms baseline, NCCL stalls at normal noise floor, error rate <0.1%. Rolling close.

sasha: assigning postmortem: eng-runtime (jamie, tariq), eng-ml (maria) and incidents lead. Required: timeline, root cause (hash change + continuous batching interaction + TP placement bug), remediation (code revert + unit tests + e2e for TP placement), detection improvement (alert for shard load skew >20% per GPU), runbook update.

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Follow-up: create postmortem ticket P-1923456789 and schedule review.

tay: noted. thanks team. handing off to oncall for watch.

sasha: thanks everyone. if anything else pops up reopen thread.
